description: Hurricane Beryl: Reconnaissance of Wind and Storm-Surge Damage to Buildings in Houston and Galveston, Texas is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "field recon", published or maintained by Dimitrios Kalliontzis, University of Houston (uh.edu). This project presents reconnaissance data collected in the aftermath of Hurricane Beryl, which made landfall on the Texas coast near Matagorda as Category 1 hurricane and hit the Houston area around 4 a.m. CDT on Monday, July 8, 2024. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "field recon" project. Keywords: Hurricane Beryl, High Wind, Storm Surge, Derecho Storm, Galveston, Houston. Published 2024-08-05. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
